title: Different NAO slopes gave no clear winter rainfall reconstruction gain in Scotland in 1981-2025
abstract: We tested whether separate rainfall slopes for positive and negative winter mean NAO improve later-winter reconstruction. We used 75 winters in 1951-2025 from fixed Met Office and NOAA snapshots. Fits used only earlier years and scored 45 winters in 1981-2025. Scotland was the primary test. Adding absolute mean NAO raised mean squared error by 0.69%; RMSE rose from 92.11 to 92.43 mm. The conditional 95% five-winter block interval for error reduction was -4.72% to +3.79%. England and Wales also had negative point gains. The full-sample Scottish positive-minus-negative slope difference was +46.43 mm per NAO unit, with row-block limits -12.81 to +123.83. The data give no clear accuracy gain for this change in slope. They do not prove equal physical response or assess advance forecasts. One index, country means, revised data, model choice and short tests limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, numerical checks and a figure are included. External source records and per-winter derivatives stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Separate positive and negative NAO slopes gave no clear added Scottish accuracy in 1981-2025. Full-sample slope contrasts were also uncertain. Limits depend on the stated block resampling assumptions.

citations.reason: Verified monthly-term benchmark informed the new sign-dependent slope test. Source records overlap.
